chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiyah ibn Wahb, from Zurarah, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, concerning a matter which the seeker asks from his Lord.

He said: "He gives charity during his day to sixty needy persons, for each needy person one sa' according to the sa' of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. Then when night comes, he performs ghusl in the second third of the night, and he wears the humblest of what he wears." And he mentioned the hadith until he said: "Then when he raises his head in the second sajdah, he performs istikharah of Allah one hundred times, saying..." and he mentioned the supplication.
Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: The ghusl of the night of the middle of Sha'ban is sunnah (recommended prophetic practice).

key_terms.اسْتَخَارَ: He seeks the good from Allah through istikharah.
key_terms.الدُّعَاءَ: The supplication recited in this devotional act.
key_terms.السَّجْدَةِ: The prostration in which the supplication practice occurs.
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: A recommended prophetic practice, not an obligation.
key_terms.صَاعٌ: A prophetic measure of food given to each needy person.
key_terms.مِسْكِينًا: A needy person receiving the charitable measure.
key_terms.يَتَصَدَّقُ: He gives charity as part of the devotional act.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith prescribe for someone seeking a matter from Allah, and what is the ruling on the ghusl of mid-Sha'ban night?
ai.summary: This report describes a devotional practice for one seeking a matter from Allah, involving charity, ghusl, humble clothing, sajdah, and repeated istikharah with supplication. It concludes with a juristic note that the ghusl of the night of mid-Sha'ban is sunnah (recommended prophetic practice).
